subject: Discovery recap & proposal: swing-slot demo playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Becker <alex.becker@novamed.com>, Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & proposal: swing-slot demo playbook

Hi Alex + Jordan —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same context:
- Primary use case: low-latency inference for clinical summarization pipelines (p99 latency target ~120ms).
- Data & security: PHI will be in scope; Novamed requires VPC/private deployment and customer KMS.
- Success criteria: 1) sub-150ms median latency on 2k qps, 2) SOC2 evidence and audit log ingestion, 3) cost target <$0.015/1k tokens.

Next steps we discussed:
1) technical deep dive + demo with infra/security stakeholders (90 mins)
2) share a mutual action plan and procurement checklist
3) surface a rotating meeting cadence that respects US/EU/APAC availability so the same stakeholders can rotate in without repeated re-runs.

Scheduling ask: Novamed has distributed stakeholders (US ops, EU R&D, APAC security). To avoid repeatedly missing people, we propose a "swing-slot" rotation where the demo time shifts weekly across three windows so each region gets a friendly local time every third week. Proposed windows (converted to local examples):
- US-friendly window (Week U): 08:00–09:30 PT / 11:00–12:30 ET (good for US ops)
- EU-friendly window (Week E): 15:00–16:30 CET / 14:00–15:30 BST (good for EU R&D)
- APAC-friendly window (Week A): 23:00–00:30 JST / 22:00–23:30 SGT (early morning US, late evening APAC)

Example rotation (start date options below):
- Week of Aug 16: US window (Aug 16 — prefer Mon/Tue AM PT)
- Week of Aug 23: EU window
- Week of Aug 30: APAC window

Please reply with: (A) which of the three windows works best for your core stakeholders for the next two sessions, (B) any blackout dates, and (C) whether we should invite product-security or legal to the first deep dive.

I attached high-level discovery notes and a starter MAP to align responsibilities. If you'd rather we send a Doodle/Cal poll, I can create one — or if you prefer, pick two slots and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to confirming.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary.

Quick notes from our side:
- EU R&D definitely prefers the EU window; they have limited late-evening availability.
- Jordan (APAC) is on PTO next week but said APAC can do the APAC window the week after.
- For the first deep dive, please include our head of Infosec (Priya Shah) — she needs to validate KMS and audit log ingestion.

We'd like to aim for one of these concrete slots:
- Mon Aug 16, 15:00 CET (EU window) OR
- Tue Aug 17, 08:00 PT (US window) — if that helps get US ops on the opener.

If you want to hold the rotating cadence, start with Aug 16 (EU) and rotate as you proposed. Please send invites when confirmed.

—Alex
Alex Becker

Appreciate the quick reply Alex. Two practical suggestions from our side to keep the rotation low-friction:
1) Make the first three demos concrete and send calendar invites now (so people can block far in advance) — we can set them as recurring *but* mark each occurrence as "rotating" with the local window in the title.
2) Keep the core demo content fixed (infra + security + cost), then add a 20-min breakout for region-specific questions.

Proposed concrete dates/times (converted to a single timezone block for clarity):
- Session 1 (EU window): Tue Aug 17, 15:00–16:30 CET — host: Redwood deep-dive (security + infra)
- Session 2 (US window): Tue Aug 24, 08:00–09:30 PT — host: Redwood product + cost optimization
- Session 3 (APAC window): Tue Aug 31, 23:00–00:30 JST — host: Redwood operations (we'll keep a recording for US folks)

If those dates look ok, we'll: a) create calendar invites with dial-in + recording, b) include Priya Shah and the infra leads, and c) post the MAP link in the invite.

Ben Carter
